data.name: Caietan
data.gender_notes: Caietan is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word caio, meaning 'I call.' In Christian tradition, Caietan is the name of a Portuguese saint and bishop, and the name of a town in Italy. The name Caietan carries the meaning “He who calls, invokes” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Caietan usually hope their child will grow to embody he who calls, invokes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the act of calling upon God for guidance and strength.
data.etymology: Caietan belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “He who calls, invokes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Caietan total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: St. Caietan is the patron saint of Portugal and of drunkards, and is also known as the "Lord of Miracles". He is believed to have performed numerous miracles throughout his life, and his veneration is particularly popular among the marginalized and the downtrodden. The name Caietan is thus associated with the Portuguese culture, particularly in the context of religious devotion and miraculous interventions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Caietan holds spiritual significance as it is derived from the Latin word caio, which means 'I call.' In a Christian context, this name represents the idea of calling out to God for help, protection, and guidance. The name Caietan serves as a reminder of the importance of prayer and faith in seeking God's intervention in our lives and in facing our challenges and difficulties. It also symbolizes the belief that God is always there to hear our prayers and to answer them in His own time and in His own way.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Caietan, meaning 'little one' in the Basque language, is a name given to St. Catherine of Siena, who saw herself as a humble vessel for divine love. Her spiritual strength and dedication to God's will inspired countless souls throughout history.
